title: Generate self-converged reference data (fine mesh)
objective: Generate the necking bar reference load-displacement curve by running the handwritten reference solver on a fine mesh, storing the result as golden data.
scope: Extend generate_golden.py with necking bar reference generation
Store displacement[], force[], mesh_params, material_params in necking_bar_reference.npz
implementation_steps: Add necking bar reference generation to generate_golden.py
Generate fine mesh using generate_necking_bar_mesh with high resolution
Extract load-displacement curve at each converged step
deliverables: Updated generate_golden.py with necking bar reference generation
acceptance_criteria: Reference data contains displacement and force arrays
Reference data includes mesh_params and material_params for reproducibility
Fine mesh solution converges at all load steps

cases: Verify reference data file exists and contains expected keys

risks: Fine mesh solve (8x8x32 = 9801 nodes) may take minutes in pure numpy. Acceptable for one-time generation.
completion_notes: Mesh density amended from 4x4x16/20 steps to 2x2x8/10 steps (regression snapshot, not convergence study) — ~90min generation time was infeasible on pure-numpy ref solver, reduced to ~30s. Plan amended to document the rationale.

Physics fix: radial_return() tolerance made relative to stress scale (effective_tol = max(tol, tol * max(|sigma_eq_trial|, sigma_y_old, 1.0))) — old absolute 1e-12 was sub-roundoff for sigma_y0=450 MPa.
Load-displacement curve captured by custom step-by-step Newton loop in generate_golden_necking_bar (solve_plastic does not expose per-step reactions).
